answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity verification to a cryptographic stake burning curve: registering the n-th identity vertex mandates burning stake proportional to n^2. This superlinear cost scaling enforces insurmountable economic friction, rendering attacker expansion unsustainably expensive. Like a hypervelocity comet fracturing impervious shale rock, quadratic burn burns through adversarial reserves exponentially faster than any coordinated subversion effort can yield returns.
